book.title: A Christmas Carol · Stave 3 — The Second of the Three Spirits
book.author: Charles Dickens, A Christmas Carol (1843)

iconic_quotes_kept: Come in! and know me better, man!
This boy is Ignorance. This girl is Want

cast.name: Scrooge
cast.canonical: a thin bent elderly man, completely bald on top with wispy grey side-hair, a long smooth clean-shaven face and a sharp pointed nose, in a plain striped knee-length nightshirt, barefoot, bare-headed
cast.anchor: thin bent bald clean-shaven old man, sharp nose, striped nightshirt, barefoot
cast.distinct_from: the old bald Scrooge — not a giant, not a ghost

cast.name: Ghost of Christmas Present
cast.canonical: a huge jolly giant with a broad bare chest, dark curly hair and a short curly beard, in a loose open robe trimmed with thick white fur that leaves his chest bare, a wreath of holly with little icicles on his head, holding up a bright torch shaped like a horn of plenty
cast.anchor: jolly bare-chested giant, holly-and-icicle wreath crown, horn-shaped torch, fur-trimmed open robe
cast.distinct_from: a warm crowned GIANT — never small, never skeletal; his unmistakable marks are the holly-wreath crown and the horn-shaped torch

cast.name: Tiny Tim
cast.role: Bob Cratchit's frail, sweet youngest son
cast.canonical: a very small frail sickly boy with a thin pale face and a brave sweet smile, one thin leg in an iron brace, leaning on a little wooden crutch, dressed poorly but neatly
cast.anchor: tiny frail boy, iron leg-brace, little wooden crutch, sweet smile
cast.distinct_from: a tiny disabled child with a crutch — the smallest figure

cast.name: Bob Cratchit
cast.canonical: a thin gentle clerk with dark hair and a mild kind face, wound in a long white knitted comforter scarf, in a threadbare coat
cast.anchor: thin dark-haired clerk, long white comforter scarf
cast.distinct_from: a grown thin clerk — not bald, not a giant

cast.name: Fred
cast.canonical: a cheerful handsome young man with dark side-whiskers and a small moustache, bright warm eyes, a scarf and a sprig of holly pinned to his coat
cast.anchor: cheerful young man, dark side-whiskers, holly sprig on his coat
cast.distinct_from: young and warm — not the old miser

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed old man in a striped nightshirt sitting up in bed at midnight, a strange warm blaze of light glowing under the door of the next room, drawing him toward it

teen.narration: THE BELL STRUCK ONE AGAIN, AND A STRANGE LIGHT GLOWED FROM THE NEXT ROOM.

bubbles.text: Scrooge's own room was changed — but who was waiting for him inside?

panels.scene: a huge jolly bare-chested giant with a holly-and-icicle wreath crown and a torch shaped like a horn of plenty, seated on a throne heaped with turkeys, holly, fruit, puddings and bowls of punch, in a room turned into a warm woodland grove

teen.narration: THE SECOND SPIRIT — THE GHOST OF CHRISTMAS PRESENT, A JOLLY GIANT ON A THRONE OF FOOD.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: Come in — and know me better, man!

panels.scene: the jolly bare-chested giant standing tall, his holly wreath crown and his horn-shaped torch held high, beaming warmly down at someone below

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: You have never seen the like of me before! Look upon me!
He was crowned with holly, and his torch poured warmth on all it touched.

panels.scene: the giant ghost striding over the snowy rooftops of a whole city at night, sprinkling glittering sparks from his horn-shaped torch down onto the people and their dinners below

teen.narration: THE SPIRIT CARRIED SCROOGE OUT OVER THE CITY, BLESSING EVERY DINNER WITH HIS TORCH.

bubbles.text: Wherever people were poorest, he sprinkled the most cheer of all.

panels.scene: the small plain kitchen of a poor family on Christmas Day, a thin cheerful mother and several children in worn but tidy clothes bustling to lay a modest Christmas dinner, a tiny fire

teen.narration: THEY CAME TO THE HOME OF BOB CRATCHIT, SCROOGE'S POOR CLERK.

bubbles.text: Mrs Cratchit and the children were laying their small Christmas dinner with great pride.

panels.scene: the thin dark-haired clerk in his long white comforter scarf carrying his youngest son home on his shoulder — a very small frail boy with a little wooden crutch and one leg in an iron brace

teen.narration: BOB CAME HOME CARRYING HIS YOUNGEST — LITTLE TINY TIM.

bubbles.text: Frail Tim, with his crutch and iron leg-brace, was as good as gold — patient, and never once complaining.

panels.scene: the tiny frail boy with his little crutch and iron leg-brace, looking up with a sweet brave smile, a warm poor room behind him

bubbles.speaker: TINY TIM
bubbles.text: I hope the people saw me in church — I like them to remember who made lame beggars walk.

panels.scene: the whole poor family crowded happily around a small table for Christmas dinner — a little roast goose and a small flaming pudding — everyone beaming with delight

teen.narration: THE WHOLE FAMILY DELIGHTED IN THEIR SMALL, SPLENDID DINNER.

bubbles.text: There never was such a goose — and oh, what a wonderful pudding!

panels.scene: the thin dark-haired clerk in his white comforter scarf lifting a glass in a warm toast at the head of the small dinner table, his family around him

bubbles.speaker: BOB
bubbles.text: A merry Christmas to us all, my dears — God bless us!

panels.scene: the tiny frail boy with his crutch, seated close by his father's side, lifting his small face to answer, warm firelight around them

bubbles.speaker: TINY TIM
bubbles.text: God bless us, every one!

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed old man in his striped nightshirt watching the little crippled boy from the shadows, a new softness and worry on his hard face

teen.narration: SCROOGE FELT SOMETHING NEW — CONCERN FOR THE BOY.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Spirit, tell me — will Tiny Tim live?

panels.scene: the giant holly-crowned ghost looking down gravely, his torch dimmed, one great hand raised in solemn warning

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: I see a vacant seat, and a crutch without an owner. If nothing changes, the child will die.

panels.scene: the giant holly-crowned ghost leaning down sternly, his cheerful face now serious, pointing a warning finger

teen.narration: THEN THE SPIRIT THREW SCROOGE'S OWN CRUEL WORDS BACK AT HIM.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: 'Decrease the surplus population'? Take care WHO you call surplus — if you have a heart, and not a stone.

panels.scene: the thin dark-haired clerk in his white comforter scarf raising his glass again at the little table, kindly, though his tired wife beside him looks cross
panels.composition: close — a toast to the hard master

teen.narration: BOB EVEN DRANK TO HIS HARD MASTER.

bubbles.speaker: BOB
bubbles.text: To Mr Scrooge — the Founder of the Feast!
Mrs Cratchit's face fell. 'The Founder of the Feast, indeed!' she said.

panels.scene: a bright warm parlour where a crowd of cheerful young guests laugh and play a party game, a handsome young man with dark side-whiskers and a holly sprig laughing warmly among them

teen.narration: AT FRED'S PARTY, THE LAUGHTER WAS WARM — EVEN ABOUT UNCLE SCROOGE.

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: He told me Christmas was a humbug — ha ha! But I mean to be kind to him anyway.

panels.scene: the giant ghost now looking suddenly aged — his hair and beard turned grey, his torch burning low — near the end of his one night of life

teen.narration: AS THE NIGHT PASSED, THE SPIRIT GREW OLD, HIS HAIR TURNING GREY.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: My life upon this globe is very brief. It ends tonight.

panels.scene: the aged giant ghost opening his fur-trimmed robe to reveal two wretched, starving, ragged children — a boy and a girl — clinging to his legs, hollow-eyed and desperate

teen.narration: FROM UNDER HIS ROBE CAME TWO STARVING, RAGGED CHILDREN.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: This boy is Ignorance. This girl is Want. Beware them both — but most of all, beware this boy.

panels.scene: the aged giant ghost fading away as a great bell tolls midnight; behind him a silent, hooded, faceless phantom in a black robe begins to glide toward the viewer
panels.composition: close — midnight, and the last phantom comes

teen.narration: AS MIDNIGHT STRUCK, THE SPIRIT THREW SCROOGE'S WORDS BACK ONCE MORE — AND VANISHED.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: Are there no prisons? Are there no workhouses?
The clock struck twelve — and a silent, hooded phantom came gliding toward Scrooge.
